altbuild: run.sh altbuild rebuilds the same pinned source with CXXFLAGS="-O3 -std=c++17 -mfma -ffp-contract=fast" against MFEM's own OPTIM_FLAGS of -O3 -std=c++17 (config/defaults.mk:29, taken by CXXFLAGS ?= $(OPTIM_FLAGS) at makefile:227). Enabling FP contraction is something a correct candidate on this hardware could plausibly be built as, and it is chosen over -O0 deliberately: on baseline x86_64 gcc -O0 changes nothing in floating-point evaluation, so it would record a floor of exactly zero, which is evidence that the alternative build computed the same thing rather than evidence of stability (references/pitfalls/altbuild-floors-are-host-specific.md).

warrant: A pure description of the loaded mesh with no numerics at all, which makes it the cheapest statement in the module that the mesh was read as upstream reads it. Counts and degrees are integers and compare exactly; the knot vectors compare pointwise. This stream is written at the C++ default of six significant digits -- the source sets no precision on it -- so one printed unit is 1e-6 relative for values below 1 and 1e-5 for values in [1,10), and the bound on it is rtol 2e-5, two printed units, never the 1e-6 that fits an eight-digit field. The bound is atol 1e-07 with rtol 2e-05, finalized with the human at STOP 4 from the 2026-09-11 calibration run and revised on the curator's review of PR #647, which measured the actual digit count of every graded stream. Every graded stream of this check is written at the C++ default of six significant digits -- the source sets no precision on it -- so one printed unit is 1e-6 relative for values below 1 and 1e-5 for values in [1,10). A bound may not sit below one printed unit (references/pitfalls/output-precision-floors-the-bound.md), so rtol is 2e-5, two printed units at worst, and not the 1e-6 that fits an eight-digit field. The calibration run measured the nominal-versus-variant spread of all twenty checks: 1e-9 to 1e-6, with two checks (derham-interpolators at 2.17e-8 and maxwell-definite at 2.00e-8) exceeding the provisional atol of 1e-8 because their reference values are small enough that the rtol term contributes little; raising atol one decade fixed that. Every measured spread is an exact multiple of 1e-9 or 1e-8, i.e. the print quantised it, so the margins are bound over print quantum. Shrinking the variant instead was rejected: at 1e-10 the perturbation moves 5 of 4225 values and at 1e-12 none at all. A real port fault -- a wrong rational basis, a dropped weight, a mis-scaled penalty on the weak boundary term, a geometry that moves under refinement -- shifts these outputs by 1e-3 or more on a state of order one, two to four orders above the bound, so the bound is loose enough for a legitimate build and far tighter than any meaningful fault.
